Ask a question About Alchemist What is Alchemist? Alchemist is an early-stage venture firm that backs deeply technical teams building for the enterprise, then guides them to enterprise traction. We invest at pre-seed and seed. Every founder in our portfolio benefits from our Founder experience . Highlights include an equity-aligned Partner matched to their company, a proven enterprise method built on playbooks refined over fourteen years, the Vault with our network of 40,000 mentors, over $500K in perks, and a community of founders that stays with them for the long haul. Alchemist was founded by Ravi Belani in 2012 and is based in San Francisco. We have made more than 750 investments, with founders from 60+ countries. How is Alchemist different from Techstars, Y Combinator and
How is Alchemist different from Techstars, Y Combinator and other accelerators?
Alchemist no longer considers itself an accelerator.
We are an early-stage venture firm, and our focus is guiding deeply technical teams to enterprise traction.
How is Alchemist different from other early-stage venture firms?
We back deeply technical researchers, engineers and domain experts building the next generation of enterprise infrastructure and technology.
Their business model is B2B, and they can be in any sector.
What sets us apart is what happens after we invest.

Every portfolio company gets: An equity-aligned Partner matched to your company A Founder Plan, built with you when we invest A Success Manager matched to your company A proven enterprise method, refined over fourteen years Digital investor materials that we share broadly with our global investor network The Vault, with 40,000 connections to tap into Learn more about our Founder experience .
We also run programs in Chicago with the Polsky Center at the University of Chicago, in Doha with QRDI Council, and in Tokyo.
Is Alchemist still Alchemist Accelerator?
Alchemist no longer calls itself Alchemist Accelerator.
We are the same firm and the same team that founders have known since 2012, and our legal entity is still Alchemist Accelerator, LLC.

Spotify Apple Podcasts YouTube Host Ian Bergman Share In this episode of the Innovators Inside Podcast, Marcelo Calbucci joins the show to break down how Amazon’s PR FAQ framework and a narrative-driven innovation culture can help founders, corporate innovators, and product leaders make smarter decisions and build solutions customers truly care about. With experience at Microsoft, Amazon, and six startups, Marcelo offers practical insights that apply to anyone trying to innovate in today’s fast-changing environment. Here are the five key takeaways from their conversation: 1. Start With Real Customer Problems, Not Ideas Marcelo emphasizes a core truth that many innovators skip. Successful innovation begins with understanding a real customer problem. That means going deeper than surface-level assumptions and quantifying frequency, urgency, alternatives, and the value

Fast iteration unlocks two things: Clearer signals on what actually works Reduced waste from overbuilding or planning too far ahead Whether you are a founder or driving change inside an enterprise, the lesson is the same.
AI Is a Superpower When Used as a Thinking Partner One of the most forward-looking parts of the discussion is Marcelo’s optimism about AI.
He believes AI will accelerate breakthroughs in health, energy, education, and everyday productivity.
AI should not replace thinking.
Using AI as an editor, a research assistant, or a tool for exploring blind spots can dramatically improve decision-making.
Outsourcing strategy to AI, however, leads to generic thinking and poor outcomes.

His approach blends discipline, creativity, and real-world experience, and the lessons in this episode offer a roadmap for anyone trying to innovate inside a startup, an enterprise, or anywhere in between.

Demo Day, Class 4 It started in 2012 with Ravi Belani, then a venture capitalist at DFJ, hosting founder events in San Francisco. Enterprise founders kept telling him the same thing: they did not need millions of dollars to get started. They needed a small check and a program built for them, at a time when the best-known accelerators were designed for consumer apps. So he carved out a home for that group: Alchemist, an accelerator built only for enterprise founders and backed by DFJ, Khosla Ventures, US Venture Partners, Cisco and SAP. Alchemist strength in community Danielle D'Agostaro joined as co-founder in 2013. Together they brought in the best Partners in the industry to keep developing sales methodologies built specifically for the enterprise, work that became our playbooks and, later, published books.
